issue.title: feat(id): bounded raw input token assembler (inert, #787 slice B)
issue.body:
Slice B of the landed #787 design (`doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §4.2 and §6 row B).

Part of #787. This is one of six slices and does not close the issue; C–F remain.

## What this adds

A new, **inert** Rust module `pkgs/id/src/input_framing.rs` (plus its registration in
`src/lib.rs`) that turns arbitrary transport chunks into complete logical key tokens:

- Retains an incomplete UTF-8 scalar, CSI or SS3 sequence across `push` calls and
  emits one token per complete key, independent of how the transport split the bytes.
  Plain text emits one token per Unicode scalar.
- Token bytes are never rewritten; what the assembler emits is exactly what the
  transport received, so the durable `Input(Vec<u8>)` boundary is untouched.
- Bounds: 256-byte cap per pending token and a 5-second incomplete-token deadline
  (§4.2 safety defaults). Overlong tokens, invalid UTF-8, incomplete tokens at
  EOF/deadline and queue loss are fatal; the caller must close the session, because
  a missing prefix cannot be resynchronised.
- Connection-local state: one `InputAssembler` per raw connection, so interleaved
  connections cannot mix partial tokens.
- `ReplyFilter` seam only: `push_filtered` drops recognized control replies while
  preserving key order, for F13.4's demultiplexer to implement in slice E. No filter
  is provided that swallows unrecognized keys.

**No activation.** `world_ssh` does not call the module, the durable `Input` event,
journal format, guest ABI, browser encoder and lease/negotiation paths are unchanged.

## Tests

```
cd pkgs/id && cargo test --lib input_framing::tests
# 16 passed; 0 failed
```

Coverage follows the §6 done check: every split point and byte boundary of the fixture
corpus, coalesced keys, split probe-reply + key order, cap boundary (exactly 256 passes,
257 fails), unterminated over-cap, deadline, EOF with/without pending bytes, invalid
UTF-8 and overlong forms, malformed escapes, queue loss and interleaved connections.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. Default-feature targeted crate tests pass (16/16),
and `cargo check --all-targets` passes with the crate's default features. The isolated
module also passes `clippy-driver` with the crate's Clippy groups and repo-specific
allow-list. Both `cargo clippy --lib` and `cargo clippy --lib --all-features` could not
complete: they failed with `E0514` incompatible-compiler metadata errors in existing
dependency artifacts (e.g. `p2panda_core`, `thiserror`, `anyhow`) before reaching the
crate lint pass. `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` also cannot compile in this
checkout because the RustEmbed input `web/dist` has not been generated. The
`--no-default-features` test variant cannot compile on current `main` because of
pre-existing `world`/`petname` feature-gated references in `chat.rs`/`invite.rs`; the
default-feature test variant passed.

No automated CI jobs were triggered for this PR. `.github/workflows/id-check.yml` has
only `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers (its header still mentions PRs), so
package-level PR CI coverage is absent on this branch; the required code check was run
locally as described above. `roc-test` passes all 83 Roc expectations.

## Slice status after this PR

- A — merged (#4438)
- **B — this PR (inert)**
- C (browser encoder) and D (parity oracle) — next, independent/inert
- E/F — still gated on F13.4 detection (#786)

issue.body:
Part of the worlds design program: [#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955). Statements S73–S74 of the 2026-11-04 brief. Filed as dedicated research per Drew's rule for sub-parts needing their own documentation.

## Task (Drew, in substance)

We need **a basic system to convert images and videos into the kitty protocol**, and there are also **IDF video-to-ASCII tools** out there — some of those might be used as well. Survey what exists before building anything:

- **Kitty graphics protocol**: encoder/tooling landscape (library support, terminal support matrix), stills vs animation/video over the protocol, bandwidth and chunking behavior.
- **Adjacent terminal graphics**: sixel, iTerm2 inline images — only insofar as the fallback tiers need them.
- **Video-to-ASCII**: the IDF tools Drew names and the wider field (jp2a-style stills pipelines, `mpv` ASCII outputs, dedicated converters) — quality, speed, color fidelity, licensing (this feeds the licensing program too: a converter's license constrains bundling).
- Where conversion should live: upload-time (presentation-layer conversion tools, per the assets design child of [#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955)), client-side at render time, or both for different tiers.

## Not this

[#787](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/787) is the kitty **keyboard** protocol on the raw input path — a different protocol that happens to share the terminal. This research is graphics/media only; don't merge the two.

## Done looks like

A research doc: tooling survey with licenses, a recommended converter pipeline per tier (kitty graphics / ASCII video / static ASCII), and the conversion-placement decision with reasons.

issue.title: queue: no reconciliation between open issues and queue coverage — non-creator filings never get queue items

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: app/fleet
labels.description: pkgs/fleet multicall binary + platform crates

issue.body:
## Problem

Nothing reconciles the open-issue set against the fleet queue. Issues enter the queue only when a creator-class lane files them (file + enqueue in the same pass). Issues filed any other way — by work lanes filing blockers mid-task, by audit lanes, by hand, or predating the queue (epics) — silently never get a queue item, so no lane ever dispositions them.

## Evidence — reconciliation run 2026-11-07 (Drew's question: "did you import all open issues without a queue item?")

Method: full open-issue enumeration via gh REST (PRs excluded) for the four fleet repos; full fleet-queue scan of the four pilot queues (8,493 tasks) matched on dedupe keys `repo-health:v1:(fix|triage):<repo>:issue:<n>` incl. dispatch-suffixed variants and legacy repo-name aliases.

| repo | open | live task | done-task only | NO task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| developing-today/code | 1,347 | 656 | 676 | **15** |
| developing-today-forks/opencode | 95 | 44 | 45 | **6** |
| developing-today-forks/openchamber | 95 | 59 | 36 | 0 |
| dezren39/darwin-nix | 30 | 19 | 9 | **2** |

The 23 uncovered issues were imported the same day as triage tasks 11424–11446 (all verified in-store; several already claimed within minutes). They include today's own filings (#6884, #6935, #6942, #6944, #6985, #6992, #6994), home-cluster epics (#1083, #1104–#1106), fork pr-shepherd items (opencode #1715, #1757, #1947), and darwin-nix #11/#1637 — proof the gap is structural, not one lane's miss: any filing path that isn't a creator run leaks.

The 766 "done-task only" issues (worked, issue still open) are a separate, larger lag class — triage/fix tasks complete without the issue closing — flagged here for visibility, not as part of this fix.

## Fix

1. Standing reconciliation: run this exact diff (open issues vs pilot-queue dedupe coverage) on a cadence (the hourly orchestration pass or its own job) and auto-import uncovered issues as triage packets via the sanctioned enqueue path (dedupe-key idempotent by construction).
2. File-and-enqueue rule: any lane that files an issue outside a creator run enqueues its triage packet in the same pass, or records why not in the filing comment.

## Acceptance

- A scheduled reconciliation exists and its first run reports 0 uncovered open issues across the four repos.
- The file-and-enqueue rule is written into the lane/creator runbooks it applies to.

issue.body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#218 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

opencode v2 wraps every MCP server in its own code mode unless the server is configured `codemode: false`, and this machine's v1 does the same because `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` is set. So mcpx's `/mcp` ends up as a tool called from a program the model wrote for opencode's interpreter, and nothing in mcpx's docs says to opt out. v2 also appends `?codemode=false` to remote MCP URLs so servers that bundle code mode can expose raw tools; mcpx ignores it. opencode runs permission checks and plugin hooks per child call, shows live status, and cancels on abort. The plugin's `mcpx_exec` makes one blocking POST and ignores the abort signal (the session and field bugs are #189).

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CODE-53](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-53-opencode-wraps-mcp-servers-in-code-mode-by-default) | opencode wraps MCP servers in code mode by default | ✗ — docs never tell users to opt out | S |
| [PLG-35](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md#plg-35-codemodefalse-appended-to-remote-mcp-urls) | `?codemode=false` appended to remote MCP URLs | ✗ — neither sends nor honours it | M |
| [PLG-36](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md#plg-36-hooks-and-permission-checks-per-child-call-in-code-mode) | Hooks and permission checks per child call in code mode | ✗ — script calls bypass opencode permissions | L |
| [PLG-37](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md#plg-37-live-status-of-each-child-call-during-a-script) | Live status of each child call during a script | ✗ — plugin makes one blocking POST | S |
| [PLG-38](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md#plg-38-cancelling-in-the-harness-stops-the-script) | Cancelling in the harness stops the script | ✗ — plugin ignores the abort signal | S |

## What to do

Document `codemode: false` for mcpx in opencode config; decide whether `?codemode=false` should expose upstream tools flat; plumb abort and live status through the plugin's `mcpx_exec`.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** med · **Related**: #189, #47, #48

## Acceptance criteria

- mcpx documentation tells opencode users how mcpx interacts with opencode's default code-mode wrapping, including how to opt a server out (`codemode: false`) (CODE-53).
- mcpx honors `?codemode=false` on its `/mcp` URL: raw tools are exposed instead of the code-mode surface.
- The plugin's `mcpx_exec` respects the host abort signal — an aborted session cancels the in-flight call instead of blocking to completion.
- Tests cover the query-parameter handling and the abort path.

issue.body:
## Gap: the Turso queue backend has no revive/requeue verb

Found during the dead-at-cap requeue pass (2026-11-07) executing the staged evaluation in #6463 against `fleet-queue`.

**What exists:** `fleet queue` verbs on the Turso backend (`turso_queue.rs`): enqueue, claim, lane, bind, heartbeat, checkpoint, park, block, cancel, fail, complete, list, health, signal, events-*. `verb_fail` only requeues a *claimed* task on transient failure while attempts remain.

**What's missing:** any supported way to revive a `queued` task whose `attempts >= max_attempts` (the silent-zombie state #6463 is about — 231 such rows fleet-wide at the 2026-11-07 census). Specifically:

1. No `revive`/`requeue` verb that resets `attempts` (and clears `last_error`) on a queued row with an audit event.
2. `verb_enqueue`'s dedupe lookup (`WHERE queue = ? AND dedupe_key = ?`) has **no status predicate** — it returns the existing row even when that row is `cancelled`/`done`/`failed`. The PG backend's revive-on-enqueue semantics (only live rows dedupe-match) were not ported, so cancel + re-enqueue of the same packet silently returns the dead row instead of creating a fresh task.

**Impact:** the 2026-11-07 requeue pass had to reset attempts via direct SQL against fleet-queue (queued rows only, guard predicates `status='queued' AND attempts>=max_attempts`, one `revived` event row per task) because no verb path exists. Cancellations of superseded tasks did go through the `cancel` verb.

**Ask:** add a `revive` verb (task id + worker + reason → attempts=0, not_before=now or supplied, last_error=NULL, `revived` event) and make enqueue's dedupe match only non-terminal rows (reviving/resetting per the PG semantics), with tests naming the oracle (the PG migration-0023 behavior).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A supported broker verb (revive/requeue) resets attempts and clears last_error on a queued dead-at-cap task, with an audit event recorded
- [ ] Enqueue dedupe matches only live rows (queued/claimed/parked/blocked): re-enqueueing a packet whose previous row is cancelled/done/failed creates a fresh task instead of returning the terminal row
- [ ] The fleet monitor's dead-in-queue self-repair (Duty 1 addendum) can be re-pointed from direct SQL to the new verb

issue.title: feat(id): additive kitty browser encoder — #787 Slice C
issue.body: ## Summary Slice C of #787 (per `doc/2026-11-01_design_id787.md` §6 row C): adds `kittyBytesForKey`, an additive rich/kitty browser encoder, to `pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard.ts`. The legacy `terminalBytesForKey` is unchanged, and the new encoder is **unused by the UI** in this slice (inert, matching the design's phased plan; Slice F wires the opt-in). The encoder is the browser counterpart of the Slice A Roc decoder `Key.parse_events` (kitty-disambiguate-v1): - Unmodified keys keep their legacy bytes (they already decode to the same events) — except Escape, sent as CSI-u `ESC [ 27 u` because a bare ESC is `EventUnknown` to the active decoder. - Modified keys carry explicit modifiers: CSI-u for Escape/Tab/Enter/Backspace (27/9/13/127 — so Tab vs Ctrl+i and Enter vs Ctrl+m are unambiguous), `CSI 1 ; ` for arrows/Home/End, `CSI ; ~` for Delete/PageUp/PageDown, and CSI-u (not parameterised `CSI Z`, which the decoder rejects) for Shift+Tab. - Modified printable keys use CSI-u over the unshifted base scalar (lowercase letter / base digit-punctuation), mirroring a kitty terminal; AltGr (Ctrl+Alt composed non-letter, e.g. `€`) stays plain text. Meta/Dead/Process/Unidentified stay excluded. ## Tests - New tests in `world-keyboard.test.ts` assert the shared rich fixtures — each expected byte string is an `expect` line from the Roc decoder in `pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/Key.roc`, so the encoder is checked against the Slice A decoder's expectations (Slice D will replace this mirroring with the compiled parity oracle). - Laptop: `bunx vitest run src/world-keyboard.test.ts` — 17/17 pass (10 legacy + 7 new); `bun run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) passes. ## Scope notes - Issue #787 is **not** closed by this slice: its acceptance criteria stay open until Slices D (parity oracle), E and F land (E/F gated on #786). This PR therefore does not carry a closing keyword. - No changes to the durable Input event, session frames, or the legacy encoder. Refs #787 · queue task 12634 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
